structural.clause: §0C.17 (EC-4), FLOOR_EXEMPT: "&& (i.effect !== 'HANDOFF' || (i.target?.class === 's'  // a surface, not an act  && !CONSENT(i.handoff_capability_ref)  // §0B.20 — never waived  && !IDENTITY(i.handoff_capability_ref)));  // §0B.25 — never waived", and the sentence §0C.17-ter builds on it: "CONSENT and IDENTITY (§0B.20, §0B.25) are now explicit exclusions from the predicate, so no consent or identity handoff is ever exempt, whatever its priority."
structural.conflictsWith: §0B.20, which declares the predicate's domain: "Define, over RegisteredActionCapabilityV1: CONSENT(cap) := cap.targetKind ∈ {'client_consent','client_consent_security'} ∨ cap.actionClass ∈ {'record_client_consent','invalidate_client_consent_authority'}"; and §0B.25: "IDENTITY(cap) := cap.targetKind ∈ {auth_session, auth_subject_sessions, auth_identity} ∨ cap.actionClass ∈ {link_social_auth_identity, revoke_other_auth_session, revoke_all_auth_sessions}". §0C.17's own MintedIntent declaration types the argument `handoff_capability_ref: CapabilityRef | null`, and §0B.7 declares CapabilityRef as `{ space; key }` — it declares no targetKind and no actionClass member.
structural.consequence: Both exclusion conjuncts are identically true, for two independent reasons, so the exclusion can never bite. (i) Type: the predicates read members the argument's declared shape does not have; applied to a CapabilityRef, cap.targetKind and cap.actionClass are undefined and both disjuncts are false. (ii) Key space, which survives even if a registry resolution is charitably inserted: §0B.7 admits only a C9 ref on a HANDOFF ("only COMMIT and REQUEST_APPROVAL may carry an AE ref, and they may carry nothing else"), while CONSENT and IDENTITY are predicates over AE-CAP — and AE-CAP ∩ C9-CAP = ∅ (re-verified in process: zero shared spellings; CONSENT matches exactly 3 AE rows, IDENTITY exactly 6, all AE-CAP). Consequently every intent with priority 0, effect HANDOFF and target.class 's' is FLOOR_EXEMPT and floors at ANONYMOUS, including CONSENT_STATE.change_handoff_intent and IDENTITY_BINDING.bindings[].manage_handoff_intent, and including any handoff naming one of §0.37's eight reserved consent/identity acts once one is registered under §0.37's gate — §A1.6.2 establishes that four of the eight already have live, ALLOW, authenticated_request-reachable AE owners under different names. §0C.18's "Exactly five intents satisfy FLOOR_EXEMPT" is therefore a statement about today's clause set rather than a property of the derived predicate, which is exactly what §0C.17-ter rules out ("A fence that holds because no current clause exercises the hole is not a fence"), and it makes §0C.32's audit promise — "A reader auditing this contract should be able to find every floor reduction it makes by reading this table. There are two." — incomplete for the EC-4 row. This is NOT a security-contract violation: a HANDOFF never invokes its destination (R3.5.3), §0.31's routes re-check the principal proof at EP-FETCH, and §0.27's mint fence (every non-escape intent on CONSENT_STATE/IDENTITY_BINDING must derive ≥ SESSION_VERIFIED) refuses such an envelope rather than emitting it — but it fails closed by making a kind the contract requires to be mintable unmintable, which is the same shape of defect EC-4 exists to remove.
structural.fix: Make the exclusion evaluable on the value actually passed. Either (a) resolve before testing and state the space — exempt a HANDOFF only when `i.handoff_capability_ref.space === 'C9'`, and for any future AE-space handoff require `!CONSENT(actionCapabilityRegistry.tryGet(i.handoff_capability_ref.key)) && !IDENTITY(...)` with a fail-closed branch when tryGet returns undefined; or (b), better, key the exclusion on the property that exists in the space a HANDOFF may actually carry: `WIDGET_CAPABILITY_POLICY[capKey(i.handoff_capability_ref)].consent_class ∉ {'personal_data','identity_binding'}`, with an undefined row refusing the exemption. Then correct §0C.18 to state the admission rule rather than a count, and correct §0C.32's EC-4 row to describe the derived set instead of five named intents.

structural.clause: §0C.22 (EC-6), A-2 (amended) and its stated mechanism, in one paragraph: "A control's accessible name is composed as nameSourceOf(ref).label + ', ' + *the composition given by its kind's row in §4.8.2*, where §4.8.2 supplies a row, and is nameSourceOf(ref).label verbatim otherwise ... *Mechanism:* a CI check over each emitted A11yBlock asserting, for every ref ∈ a11y.reading_order, that a11y.accessible_names[refKey(ref)].startsWith(nameSourceOf(ref, env).label), and, for every kind §4.8.2 names, equality with the row's composition applied to the emitted body."
structural.conflictsWith: Itself, and §4.8.2 as amended. (a) The composition rule makes the emitted name `label + ', ' + composition`; the second conjunct of the same CI check requires that name to EQUAL `composition`. §1.1 declares Cell.label "M — ≤ 160 chars, always a human sentence fragment" and §3.1 declares WidgetIntent.label server-minted and never client-composed, so the prefix is never empty and the two conjuncts are unsatisfiable together. (b) §4.8.2 has five content columns — role_hint, keyboard model, text alternative, live region, non-colour state — and §0B.36, which amends the table from seventeen rows to twenty-two, adds its five rows under those same five columns. There is no accessible-name column in either. Also conflicts with §0C.22's closing sentence, "§4.8.2 is the sole per-kind normative owner of the accessible name", which assigns sole ownership to a column no row declares and simultaneously contradicts A-2's own label-prefix construction.
structural.consequence: (a) The EP-BUILD assertion can never pass. Since §0B.36 made §4.8.2 total over all twenty-two kinds, "every kind §4.8.2 names" is every kind, so the check fails for every emitted envelope of every kind and the build never goes green — an assertion set that can never pass, and therefore a mechanism EC-6 names that cannot run. (b) Independently, "the composition given by its kind's row in §4.8.2" names a table cell that exists for no row. The handful of accessible-name sentences that do appear in §4.8.2 (SERVICE_SELECTOR "each option's duration and price in the accessible name", STAFF_SELECTOR, STRATEGY_OPTIONS, APPROVAL, and §0B.36's ARTIFACT "accessible name = filename + format + size_bytes") sit inside the keyboard-model and text-alternative columns as prose, are present for five kinds only, and are not a declared per-kind composition. EC-6 was raised precisely because A-2 named an identifier no shape declares (intent.utterance); its replacement names a table column no table declares. Fail-closed — a build that cannot pass ships nothing.
structural.fix: Give §4.8.2 a sixth column, `accessible_name_suffix`, populated for all twenty-two rows (§0B.36's five included) with the composition each row currently states in prose, and a declared default for the seventeen that state none. Then state the mechanism as one predicate that agrees with A-2's construction: `accessible_names[refKey(ref)] === nameSourceOf(ref, env).label + ', ' + suffixOf(KIND_REGISTRY[kind], env)` for the kinds with a suffix, and `=== nameSourceOf(ref, env).label` otherwise — from which startsWith follows by construction rather than being asserted as a second, contradicting conjunct. Amend the closing sentence to "§4.8.2 is the sole per-kind normative owner of the accessible-name suffix".

structural.clause: §0C.22 (EC-6), A-2 (amended): "A control's accessible name is composed as `nameSourceOf(ref).label` + `', '` + ... and is `nameSourceOf(ref).label` **verbatim** otherwise" — two invocations, each with arity 1.
structural.conflictsWith: §0C.22-ter, which declares the function: "function nameSourceOf(ref: InteractiveRef, env: WidgetEnvelope): NameSource { const el = resolveInteractive(env, ref); ... }" — arity 2, with `env` required because the body passes it to `resolveInteractive(env, ref)`. The Mechanism line of the very same A-2 paragraph and §0C.22-ter's closing invariant both write `nameSourceOf(ref, env)`, and §0C.13's EC-6 errata row also names it as `nameSourceOf(ref, env)`.
structural.consequence: The normative sentence that defines how an accessible name is composed — the sentence the whole of EC-6 exists to write — invokes a declared function with a missing required argument, so the composition it specifies cannot be constructed as written. This is the defect class §0C.11-bis states as a rule of the section ("A normative clause must not name an identifier no shape declares") and the same class round 5 confirmed for c9Capability's `domain` argument. The referent of the missing argument is obvious and the fix is textual, but as written the clause is not evaluable and, unlike the Mechanism line beside it, does not agree with the declaration.
structural.fix: Write `nameSourceOf(ref, env).label` in both occurrences in A-2's body, matching the Mechanism line, §0C.22-ter's declaration and invariant, and §0C.13's EC-6 row.

CLOSES THE FOUR-CLAUSE CONFLICT; ITS CONSENT/IDENTITY EXCLUSION IS INOPERATIVE. The defect is real: §4.5.4 step 1 withholds every intent below the floor before step 4's PIN, while SOURCE.3 says reconnect_intent is "the only interactive element retained" below that floor, SETTINGS.4/FORM.4/FORM.6 say editor_handoff_intent and discard_intent "survive EVERY step", §0.25/§3.12.6 say the escape is never dropped on five kinds whose KIND_FLOOR is SESSION_VERIFIED, and STRATEGY.1 pins the no-action option — with no reachable_via, so §4.5.5 C4 fires and the emission fails. Round 7's repair holds — keeping subjectFloor for every non-HANDOFF exempt intent means control.run.cancel stays at its own CONTROL_FLOOR BOUND_CLIENT, and §0C.17-bis's amendment giving reconnect_intent priority 0 makes the set derivable rather than prose-only. ON THE TASK'S HARDEST QUESTION — can FLOOR_EXEMPT (SAFE_PIN) ever carry an actuating intent? REFUTED, twice over. First, the effect clause admits only NONE, REFINE, CONTROL and HANDOFF, so DRAFT, REQUEST_APPROVAL and COMMIT — §A2.2's actuating set — are excluded, and the BUILD VETO restates it independently so a later widening of the effect list cannot silently admit one; effect and priority are both server-set members of WidgetIntent composed server-side, so an author cannot promote an intent into the set. Second, and independently, the capability clause admits only capability === null, a CONTROL ref (closed at three keys), or a C9 ref whose resourceClass is 'LOCAL' — and I confirmed in process that |{c ∈ C9_CAPABILITIES : c.resourceClass === 'LOCAL'}| = 1, the single row being c9.no_action with mode READ, so EC-4's escape hatch is a structural property and not a name on a list. Since §0B.7 forbids any of those four effect classes from carrying an AE ref, and actuation requires an AE key at Gate 14, no exempt intent can reach an actuating edge. BUT the HANDOFF branch returns a flat ANONYMOUS, and the CONSENT/IDENTITY exclusions meant to keep consent and identity handoffs out of that branch are applied to a CapabilityRef while §0B.20/§0B.25 declare them over RegisteredActionCapabilityV1 — identically true, and doubly so because a HANDOFF may carry only a C9 ref while the predicates are over AE-CAP (structural finding 3). DIRECTION: it DOES lower a floor, deliberately and disclosed, but the derived set it lowers is larger than the five §0C.18 enumerates and larger than §0C.32's table records. It admits no capability, widens no allowlist, and relaxes no veto that exists — but the CONSENT/IDENTITY exclusion it presents as a veto is not one.

structural.clause: §0C.10 (S0C.10): `function c9Floor(ref: CapabilityRef): VerificationLevel { const cap = c9Registry.tryGet(ref.key); … const row = WIDGET_CAPABILITY_POLICY[ref]; … MAYA_AI_TOOL_CATALOG_BY_NAME.get(ref.key) … }`
structural.conflictsWith: §0B.31 line 937, which is NOT amended by Section 0-C and therefore stands: `switch (ref.space) { … case 'C9': return c9Floor(ref.key); … }`; and §0C.11(2)'s own build assertion, which also passes a bare key: `∀ key ∈ C9-CAP : c9Floor(key) ≥ C9_FLOOR_BASELINE[key]`.
structural.consequence: EC-2 declares c9Floor over `CapabilityRef` while both of its call sites pass a `string`. There is no reading under which the function works. (a) If the declared parameter type governs, the dispatcher and the build assertion are type errors. (b) If the call sites govern and `ref` is a string, then `ref.key` is `undefined`, `c9Registry.tryGet(undefined)` misses `C9_CAP_BY_KEY` (declared `ReadonlyMap<string, C9Capability>` over `C9_CAPABILITIES`, verified 56 rows), and the FAIL-CLOSED branch `if (cap === undefined) return 'STEP_UP_VERIFIED'` fires for ALL 56 C9-CAP keys. Either way `verificationFloor()` — FR-4's one named mechanism under §0.55 and §0B.28 — returns the unreachable `STEP_UP_VERIFIED` for every REFINE, DRAFT, HANDOFF and class-'c' NAVIGATE in the system. P-12 is `[ABSENT]` (verified: stepUp/step_up/mfa/otp/twoFactor all 0 hits), so every such intent is withheld at §4.5.4 step 1, none has a `reachable_via`, and §4.5.5 C4 converts the emission into a LIMITATION/HANDOFF-only envelope. That is verbatim the consequence §0C.9 calls 'the first-ranked structural defect' — reproduced by EC-2's own repair. §0C.11(2)'s no-lowering assertion cannot catch it, because `STEP_UP_VERIFIED ≥ C9_FLOOR_BASELINE[key]` holds for every key.
structural.fix: Pick one type and make all three sites agree. Simplest: keep the C9 branch keyed on the string, i.e. declare `function c9Floor(key: string)`, read `c9Registry.tryGet(key)` and `MAYA_AI_TOOL_CATALOG_BY_NAME.get(key)`, and replace `WIDGET_CAPABILITY_POLICY[ref]` per the fix to the next finding. Alternatively amend §0B.31's dispatcher to `case 'C9': return c9Floor(ref);` and amend §0C.11(2)'s assertion to `∀ key ∈ C9-CAP : c9Floor({space:'C9', key}) ≥ C9_FLOOR_BASELINE[key]`. Either way state the choice in §0C.13's EC-2 row so a third site cannot drift again.

structural.clause: §0C.10: `const row = WIDGET_CAPABILITY_POLICY[ref];` and §0C.28-bis (EC-11, Gate 6's second C9 branch): `else → WIDGET_CAPABILITY_POLICY[ref] must exist (else refuse)`.
structural.conflictsWith: §0B.7 ('every row key of `WIDGET_CAPABILITY_POLICY` … typed `CapabilityRef`, never `string`') and §0B.32 ('`WIDGET_CAPABILITY_POLICY` is keyed on `CapabilityRef`'), read against §0C.22-bis's own doctrine, stated one section earlier: '`InteractiveRef` is an object type and cannot key a Record, so the key form is declared' — which then declares `type InteractiveRefKey` and `declare function refKey(ref): InteractiveRefKey`.
structural.consequence: `CapabilityRef` is an object type (`{ space; key }`). No injective key function is declared for it anywhere in the contract — there is no `capKey` counterpart to `refKey`. Bracket-indexing a Record with an object coerces it to the string '[object Object]', so `WIDGET_CAPABILITY_POLICY[ref]` either returns `undefined` for every ref or collides all 56 refs onto one row. In `c9Floor` the result is `row === undefined ⇒ 'STEP_UP_VERIFIED'` for all 56 C9-CAP keys — the same total withholding as the previous finding, reached independently, so fixing one does not fix the other. In EC-11's Gate 6 branch the result is that the nine non-catalogue C9 keys are refused unconditionally, which EC-2 and §0C.11(5) exist to prevent. This is exactly the class of defect round 7 confirmed against `MAYA_AI_TOOL_CATALOG_BY_NAME` (ReadonlyMap bracket-indexed) and §0C.22-bis repaired for `InteractiveRef`; it was not carried to the capability tables.
structural.fix: Declare the key form alongside §0C.11-bis's other accessors, exactly as §0C.22-bis does for refs: `type CapabilityRefKey = `${CapabilitySpace}:${string}`; declare function capKey(ref: CapabilityRef): CapabilityRefKey` (total over the four-member closed `CapabilitySpace` union and injective because ':' is the only separator), retype the table as `Readonly<Record<CapabilityRefKey, WidgetCapabilityPolicyRow>>`, and read it as `WIDGET_CAPABILITY_POLICY[capKey(ref)]` at both sites.

'ANONYMOUS' : subjectFloor(subjectCapability(i));` — and §0C.17-ter's rule: 'NEVER waive a subject's OWN floor: control.run.cancel is CONTROL_FLOOR BOUND_CLIENT and stays there … Keeping `subjectFloor` for every non-`HANDOFF` exempt intent removes the question entirely.'

structural.clause: §0C.17, `FLOOR_EXEMPT`: `&& (i.effect !== 'HANDOFF' || (i.target?.class === 's' && !CONSENT(i.handoff_capability_ref) && !IDENTITY(i.handoff_capability_ref)));`
structural.conflictsWith: §0B.20, which declares the predicate over a different type entirely — 'Define, **over `RegisteredActionCapabilityV1`**: `CONSENT(cap) := cap.targetKind ∈ {…} ∨ cap.actionClass ∈ {…}`' — and §0B.25 likewise for `IDENTITY(cap)`; and §0C.17 itself, which declares `MintedIntent.handoff_capability_ref: CapabilityRef | null`.
structural.consequence: `CapabilityRef` declares exactly two members, `space` and `key`. It has no `targetKind` and no `actionClass`, so `CONSENT(i.handoff_capability_ref)` and `IDENTITY(i.handoff_capability_ref)` read undefined members and are FALSE for every intent. The exclusion is inert by type. It is inert a second time even under the charitable reading that the ref is resolved first: §0B.7 fixes `handoff_capability_ref` on a `HANDOFF` to a **C9** ref, while `CONSENT`/`IDENTITY` range over **AE-CAP**, and §0B.8 verifies `AE-CAP ∩ (C9-CAP ∪ TOOL-DEF) = ∅` (I re-verified the three CONSENT members and six IDENTITY members are all AE keys). So no value that can legally occupy that field can ever satisfy either predicate. Consequence: §0B.20's normative sentence — 'The only widget affordance for a consent decision is a `HANDOFF` of class `s` to `shell.privacy` with `verification_floor ≥ SESSION_VERIFIED`' — and §0C.17 cannot both be satisfied for a `priority: 0` consent handoff, because FLOOR_EXEMPT returns `ANONYMOUS` for it. §2.6.1 CHOICE.2 expressly permits such a handoff on a kind that §0.27's mint fence does not cover, and §3.5 R3.5.1 is vacuous (EB-4: all eight `NEVER_CHAT_ACTUATED` names resolve in no space), so nothing else re-imposes the floor. This is not a security violation today only because the five base shell routes are `[ABSENT]` and §3.5 R3.5.4 refuses to emit a handoff whose target has no live surface — fail-closed, and I state that as the reason rather than claiming a fence.
structural.fix: Pass the resolved capability, and resolve it in the space the field actually holds. Either (i) retype the guard to operate on refs — `const CONSENT_REF = (r: CapabilityRef | null) => r !== null && r.space === 'AE' && CONSENT(actionCapabilityRegistry.tryGet(r.key))`, and add the C9-side counterpart the field can really carry: a build-checked `C9_CONSENT_KEYS` / `C9_IDENTITY_KEYS` set that §0.37's registration gate must populate before any consent or identity key may be emitted; or (ii) drop the capability test and exclude by consent class, which is total over C9-CAP: `WIDGET_CAPABILITY_POLICY[capKey(r)].consent_class ∉ {'personal_data','identity_binding'}`. Whichever is chosen, §0C.17-ter's sentence must be narrowed to what the predicate actually tests.

structural.clause: §0C.28-ter: '`c9_domain: C9Domain | null` … Non-null IFF `capability.space === 'C9'`. Derived at EP-MINT from the emitting run's registered agent domain; **on the capability-read path, where `run_ref` is null, from the resolved principal's domain**.' followed by 'A `C9` intent minted with `c9_domain === null` is refused at `EP-MINT`.'
structural.conflictsWith: §1.7 K3, which enumerates the principal exactly — `kind`, `tenantId`, `userId`, `membershipId`, `clientId`, `channelLinkId`, `branchRefs`, `staffRef`, `proofHash` — and §0C.28-ter's own sentence two lines earlier: 'A full read of the contract finds **exactly one** domain-valued member anywhere — `Correlation.agent_id` (§1.1.4)', which §0.16 E-29 makes class D 'derived by the minter from **the run's registered agent**' and §1.1.4 makes nullable precisely because 'two paths mint envelopes: a coordination run … and a registered capability read'.
structural.consequence: 'the resolved principal's domain' names a member no shape in the contract declares. I confirmed by execution that the repository agrees: `C9Principal` (src/orchestration/c9.contract.ts:197) carries no `domain`, and `C9Domain` is a four-member union declared on `C9_DOMAINS` and attached to `C9Capability.domains` and to `c9Capability()`'s second positional argument — never to a principal. So on the capability-read path there is nothing to derive `c9_domain` from, it is `null`, and the erratum's own refusal fires: every `C9`-carrying intent minted outside a coordination run is refused at `EP-MINT`. That is the whole capability-read minting path — CHOICE, SERVICE_SELECTOR, STAFF_SELECTOR, TIME_SLOT_SELECTOR, SCHEDULE, CLIENT_LIST, METRIC, REPORT, SOURCE_STATUS — and it is a second, independent reproduction of §0C.9's 'five widget kinds unemittable' consequence, introduced by EC-11 rather than closed by it.
structural.fix: Give the capability-read path a real source. The projector already knows which capability it is reading; the honest derivation is the intersection of the emitting surface's registered domain with `c9Registry.tryGet(key).domains`, chosen by a declared total function, e.g. `declare function emissionDomain(source: WidgetSource, ref: CapabilityRef): C9Domain` with a fail-closed refusal when the intersection is empty — not from the subject capability's own `domains`, which §0C.28-ter already rules out as vacuous. If no such surface domain exists, say so and mark the capability-read half `NORMATIVE-PENDING` on a new prerequisite rather than leaving the derivation naming a member that does not exist.

structural.clause: §0C.28-bis (EC-14): 'At `EP-REGISTRY-LOAD`, every `MOMENT_REGISTRY` row's `notify_pref_key` must resolve in **the notification-consent registry**, or the process does not start'.
structural.conflictsWith: EC-14's own statement of the defect it is closing: '`notify_pref_key` is a member of no declared shape **and** the "notification-consent registry" is named nowhere else in the contract'; and §0C.13's EC-14 row, which claims 'Neither the member nor the registry existed. `ProactiveProvenance.notify_pref_key` … and the closed twelve-row `MOMENT_REGISTRY` are declared, with a start-up assertion that every row's key resolves.'
structural.consequence: EC-14 closes half of its own two-part defect. It declares the member and it declares `MOMENT_REGISTRY` — but `MOMENT_REGISTRY` is the moment catalogue, not the notification-consent registry, and the notification-consent registry is still declared by no shape anywhere in the contract (I grepped every occurrence: lines 2367, 2368, 2388, 2494, 5846 — a defect statement, a ruling, the new assertion, an errata row and §4.9.3 PR3c; no declaration). The new sentence is a start-up assertion whose failure mode is 'the process does not start', evaluated against a registry that has no declared shape, no key type and no membership rule — so it cannot be evaluated, and §0C.13's claim that the erratum made PR3c constructible does not hold. PR3c's delivery-time re-read ('the adapter re-reads that key and the quiet-hours window') names the same undeclared registry.
structural.fix: Declare it in the same code block as `Moment`, with a key type and a totality rule, exactly as `MOMENT_REGISTRY` is declared: `interface NotificationConsentRow { notify_pref_key: string; consent_class: 'communication'; owner: CapabilityRef | null }` and `declare const NOTIFICATION_CONSENT_REGISTRY: Readonly<Record<string, NotificationConsentRow>>;` — and register it as a prerequisite (it is `[ABSENT]`: `MAYA_AI_TOOL_CATALOG` has no consent key, verified) so the start-up assertion is `NORMATIVE-PENDING` rather than unevaluable. P-32's component list must name it.

structural.clause: §0C.26 (EC-9): '`interface WidgetIntentSubmission { /* …the eight existing members, unchanged… */ readback_ack?: ReadbackAck; }`' where `ReadbackAck` carries '`affirmation: string; // the caller's affirmative utterance, verbatim`'.
structural.conflictsWith: §4.4.3 RT5 — 'Every persisted column of the three stores carries exactly one `ErasureClass`. *Mechanism:* a build-time test enumerates the columns of each store from the schema and fails on any column with no class or more than one. Adding a column without classifying it breaks the build.' — read with §4.4.1 (the intent-audit store holds `WidgetIntentSubmission` metadata), §4.4.3's per-field table for `WidgetIntentSubmission` as persisted, and §0.53, which extended the classification to §0.34's new fields.
structural.consequence: Section 0-C classifies every other field it adds — `IntentRecord.body_hash` AUDIT_RETAINED (§0C.26-ter), `.selection_domain` AUDIT_RETAINED (EC-15), `.c9_domain` 'Mint class D, AUDIT_RETAINED' (§0C.28-ter) — and classifies `readback_ack` nowhere. RT5's build test therefore fails and the build cannot be produced, which is the assertion-set failure mode. Worse if it is defaulted: `affirmation` is by its own comment the caller's verbatim utterance, the same class of datum as `spoken_transcript`, which §4.4.3 classifies `CONVERSATION_CONTENT` and §3.7 R3.7.1 requires erasure to remove. Defaulting `readback_ack` to AUDIT_RETAINED would leave a spoken user utterance in the intent-audit store after a conversation-erasure request, which is the exact failure §4.4.3 was written to repair ('erasure never touches IntentRecords … is withdrawn and replaced by a classification'), and would put FR-12 in the position of asserting a property its own totality test no longer covers.
structural.fix: Add the rows to §4.4.3's `WidgetIntentSubmission` table in the same place §0.53 added §0.34's: `readback_ack.readback_ref` and `readback_ack.body_hash` → `AUDIT_RETAINED` (both are opaque handles/hashes carrying no conversation content); `readback_ack.affirmation` → `CONVERSATION_CONTENT`. Note in §0C.26 that Gate 8-R's fourth condition compares `affirmation` against a closed server vocabulary at ingress and never re-reads it afterwards, so erasing it breaks no later decision — which §0.51's noun-resolver input set already requires.

structural.clause: §0C.28-bis (EC-13): '`max_commit_intents === 2 ⟹ exactly one approve/reject pair, both non-null, both carrying the SAME confirmation_of_ref.ref (the approval_ref) and the SAME AE capability; consuming either marks the other consumed`', taken with '`APPROVAL ⟹ max_commit_intents === 2`'.
structural.conflictsWith: §0.47 — '`APPROVAL.approve_intent` / `reject_intent` **may be null**, with a non-null `blocked_reason`, only for a reason that is a server fact at compose time: `state !== 'PENDING'`, the approval's TTL has passed, or `canDecide(…)` is false for the live principal' — and §0.48 — 'A capability whose owner determines that an initiator must not decide carries `capability_gap_ref: 'GAP-SEPARATION-OF-DUTIES'` and **no decision intent**' — neither of which Section 0-C voids, and both of which Section 0-C relies on (§0B.26's FR-6f restatement, carried by §0C: 'Otherwise `blocked_reason` is set per §0.47'; §0C.14: '§0.48's `GAP-SEPARATION-OF-DUTIES` remains the disposition wherever an initiator must not decide').
structural.consequence: `max_commit_intents` is a `KIND_REGISTRY` field — a per-kind constant, not a per-envelope count — so EC-13's third line has an antecedent that is true for every APPROVAL envelope, and its consequent demands both decision intents be non-null on every one of them. For an approval whose `state` is `APPROVED`, `REJECTED`, `COMPLETED` or `EXPIRED` (all declared members of §2.6.12's enum, all preserved by §0.19), and for the `GAP-SEPARATION-OF-DUTIES` case, §0.47/§0.48 require the intents to be null and EC-13 requires them non-null. Neither can be satisfied, so the envelope is unmintable — while §0.47 exists precisely to describe how such an envelope is composed, and §0B.37 row 12 gives APPROVAL a `source_bound` expiry that presumes decided approvals are rendered. The alternative reading, that the composer must mint decision controls for a decision the live principal may not make, would be a conferral, so the fail-closed branch is the only safe one and the clause is simply unsatisfiable there.
structural.fix: Key the constraint on the envelope's minted intent count, not on the registry constant: `APPROVAL ∧ |minted COMMIT intents| === 2 ⟹ exactly one approve/reject pair, both carrying the SAME confirmation_of_ref.ref and the SAME AE capability; consuming either marks the other consumed`, plus `APPROVAL ∧ |minted COMMIT intents| === 0 ⟹ blocked_reason non-null per §0.47 or capability_gap_ref === 'GAP-SEPARATION-OF-DUTIES' per §0.48`, plus a build veto `APPROVAL ⟹ |minted COMMIT intents| ∈ {0, 2}` so a lone decision control is still unmintable. Keep `APPROVAL ⟹ max_commit_intents === 2` and `kind !== 'APPROVAL' ⟹ max_commit_intents ∈ {0,1}` as the registry-level vetoes they are.

unproven.clause: §0C.11(5): 'The nine now resolve to real levels, and the five kinds §0C.9 named become emittable: `c9.no_action` → `ANONYMOUS` …; the three `SOURCE_HANDOFF` keys … → `SESSION_VERIFIED`; and the five `SOURCE_READ` keys … take whatever their own `WIDGET_CAPABILITY_POLICY` row and consent class require' — and §0C.32's EC-2 row, which enumerates the same nine reductions as 'the only floor reductions this erratum makes'.
unproven.whyUnproven: Both sentences assert an outcome the replacement mechanism cannot produce. Under either reading of structural findings 1 and 2, `c9Floor` returns `STEP_UP_VERIFIED` for all 56 C9-CAP keys — not for the nine only, and not the levels stated. So neither the reductions nor the emittability follow, `STRATEGY_OPTIONS` remains unemittable for the reason §0C.9 gives, and the enumeration in §0C.32 is not a true account of what the section changes. Neither sentence is marked `[NON-NORMATIVE]`, neither is listed in §0C.12, and EC-2's `NORMATIVE-PENDING` status (on P-11 and P-24) does not cover them: P-11 and P-24 are the floor ladder and the `CapabilityRef` type, and the defect is that the erratum's own function is ill-typed against its own call sites, which shipping P-11 and P-24 does not repair.
unproven.fix: Repair `c9Floor` per structural findings 1 and 2, then re-state both sentences over the repaired function — and add the assertion that would have caught this, which §0C.11(2)'s monotone guard cannot: `∀ key ∈ C9-CAP : c9Floor(key) === C9_FLOOR_BASELINE[key]` (equality against the pinned post-EC-2 vector, not `≥`), so that a degenerate all-`STEP_UP_VERIFIED` result fails the build instead of passing it.

unproven.clause: §0C.28-bis (EC-11): 'The second branch is not weaker than the first: `c9Capability` is the orchestrator's own admission function, it is `[EXISTS]`, and it already refuses an unregistered key, a domain mismatch and a non-`READ` mode for BI (`c9.registry.ts:178–192`).' Restated as a fence in §0C.32's EC-2 row: 'What still fences these nine: their `WIDGET_CAPABILITY_POLICY` row, `CONSENT_CLASS_FLOOR`, and — new in EC-11 — Gate 6's second C9 branch, `c9Capability`'s own admission.'
unproven.whyUnproven: I read `c9Capability` in the repository. It performs exactly three tests: `registryHash !== C9_REGISTRY_HASH`, `!def || !def.domains.includes(domain)`, and `domain === 'BUSINESS_INTELLIGENCE' && def.mode !== 'READ'`. It tests **no role, no surface, no feature and no risk tier**. The first branch — `AiToolPolicyService.assertCanExecute(principal, def)` — tests all four, and §3.9 Gate 6 and §0.15 FR-3 define Gate 6 as exactly that: 'Authority, computed from scratch … `allowedRoles`, `allowedSurfaces`, `requiredFeatures`, `riskTier !== 'restricted'`'. The second branch is therefore strictly weaker on the one property Gate 6 exists for, and the difference bites on the nine keys EC-2 has just made reachable: `b35.confirm` and `a22.configuration` are `OWNER_HANDOFF` (verified: the only two `OWNER_HANDOFF` rows in C9-CAP), `b35.preview`/`b35.status` are the marketing audience preview, and `owner_report.download`/`.status` are owner reports. I verified by execution that the catalogue's role fences are real and narrow where they apply (`staff.schedule.update` → six owner/admin/manager roles and `allowedSurfaces: ['native']` only; `expenses.create` → two roles; `notifications.appointments.update` → four), which is precisely the protection the nine do not get. The claim is not covered by a `NORMATIVE-PENDING` marking: EC-11's status is P-01 and P-26, i.e. the gateway and the dispatch, and building both would ship the weaker branch as specified rather than close the gap.
unproven.fix: Either state the weakening honestly ('the second branch tests registry membership, domain and the BI/READ rule only; it applies no role, surface, feature or risk-tier test, and the nine keys' protection is their `WIDGET_CAPABILITY_POLICY` row, `CONSENT_CLASS_FLOOR` and the owner endpoint's own lock'), or close it by adding the missing test over a table the widget layer owns: give `WIDGET_CAPABILITY_POLICY` an `allowed_roles: readonly UserRole[]` column, require it non-empty for all nine, and make Gate 6's second branch assert the live principal's role is a member — the same shape §0.23 uses for `CONTROL`, where the contract names the owner endpoint's own lock rather than a lock that does not exist.

unproven.clause: §0C.32's EC-4 row: 'The residual is `targetFloor('s')` on a handoff, and it is tolerable for a stated reason, not by assumption: a `HANDOFF` never invokes its destination capability (R3.5.3), and **§0.31's routes re-check the principal proof at `EP-FETCH`**.'
unproven.whyUnproven: §0.31 makes that re-check claim for exactly two routes — 'Both **new** routes carry `targetFloor('s') = SESSION_VERIFIED` and re-check the live principal's proof hash at `EP-FETCH` (§2.6.22 ARTIFACT.2, §2.6.21 MEDIA.3)' — namely `shell.pay` and `shell.file`. It makes no such claim for the five base routes `shell.root`, `shell.account`, `shell.connections`, `shell.privacy`, `shell.notifications`, whose only stated protection is the very `targetFloor('s') = SESSION_VERIFIED` that EC-4 waives. And the two routes that do carry the re-check are unreachable by a FLOOR_EXEMPT intent by construction: §2.6.20 PAY.2 makes `continue_intent` a `NAVIGATE` and §2.6.22 ARTIFACT.1 makes `fetch_intent` a `NAVIGATE`, and FLOOR_EXEMPT's effect clause and BUILD VETO both exclude `NAVIGATE`. So the compensating mechanism the sentence cites applies to precisely the routes the exemption cannot reach, and to none of the routes it can. The sentence is the stated justification for a floor reduction, so it is load-bearing; it is not marked `[NON-NORMATIVE]` and is not in §0C.12.
unproven.fix: Either narrow the sentence to what §0.31 supports and name the real residual ('the residual is `targetFloor('s')` on a handoff to one of the five base shell routes, which carry no `EP-FETCH` principal re-check of their own; today nothing is emitted because those routes are `[ABSENT]` and §3.5 R3.5.4 refuses a handoff with no live surface'), or extend §0.31 so the claim becomes true: require every `ShellRoute`, not only the two parameterised ones, to re-check the live principal's proof hash at `EP-FETCH` and to refuse below `SESSION_VERIFIED` at its own ingress — which is what §0C.18's general principle ('asking for the route to a surface that authenticates') already assumes.

unproven.clause: §0C.17-ter: '**A class-`s` handoff to a consent or identity act** would have had its floor zeroed too. `CONSENT` and `IDENTITY` (§0B.20, §0B.25) are now explicit exclusions from the predicate, **so no consent or identity handoff is ever exempt, whatever its priority**.'
unproven.whyUnproven: The mechanism the sentence names does not do what the sentence says, for the two independent reasons set out in structural finding 4: `CONSENT` and `IDENTITY` are declared over `RegisteredActionCapabilityV1` and are handed a `CapabilityRef | null`, which declares neither `targetKind` nor `actionClass`, so both evaluate false for every intent; and even resolved, they range over AE-CAP while §0B.7 confines a `HANDOFF`'s `handoff_capability_ref` to a C9 ref, and §0B.8's disjointness (which I re-verified by intersecting the enumerated sets) makes the test unsatisfiable by any legal value of that field. The sentence is precisely the kind §0C.1 warns against — 'A fence that holds because no current clause exercises the hole is not a fence' — except that here the fence does not hold even in principle. It is not marked `[NON-NORMATIVE]`, is not in §0C.12, and EC-4's `NORMATIVE-PENDING` status (P-11, P-19) does not cover it.
unproven.fix: Apply the fix to structural finding 4, then re-state the guarantee over the predicate that is actually tested, and bind it to §0.37's registration gate so it stays true when a consent owner is registered under its real name: 'no handoff whose `handoff_capability_ref` resolves to a row with `consent_class ∈ {personal_data, identity_binding}`, and no handoff naming a key on `C9_CONSENT_KEYS` ∪ `C9_IDENTITY_KEYS`, is ever exempt, whatever its priority' — with an `EP-BUILD` assertion over the enumerated C9-CAP set, so the claim is checkable rather than asserted.

structural.clause: §0C.10, line 1397: `function c9Floor(ref: CapabilityRef): VerificationLevel {` — EC-2's replacement, which §0C.10 introduces with "§0B.31's `c9Floor` is VOID as written and replaced".
structural.conflictsWith: Its only two call sites both pass a `string`, not a `CapabilityRef`. §0B.31, line 937: `case 'C9':      return c9Floor(ref.key);` — the dispatcher, which §0C.13's EC-2 row does NOT void (it voids "§0B.31 `c9Floor`", i.e. the body, not `subjectFloor`). And §0C.11(2), line 1471: `∀ key ∈ C9-CAP :  c9Floor(key) ≥ C9_FLOOR_BASELINE[key]          // build assertion`.
structural.consequence: Inside the new body the first statement is `const cap = c9Registry.tryGet(ref.key);`. With `ref` bound to a string, `ref.key` is `undefined`, `tryGet(undefined)` returns `undefined`, and the function returns `'STEP_UP_VERIFIED'` on the FAIL CLOSED branch for all 56 C9-CAP keys. §0B.31 and §A1.2 P-12 make `STEP_UP_VERIFIED` unreachable while P-12 is `[ABSENT]`, so every `REFINE`, `DRAFT`, `HANDOFF` and class-`c` `NAVIGATE` naming a C9 key is withheld at §4.5.4 step 1 — precisely the state §0C.9 calls "the first-ranked structural defect" (`STRATEGY_OPTIONS` unemittable, `CLIENT_LIST`, `METRIC`, `CHART`, `PROGRESS` and `ARTIFACT` permanently withheld) and which §0C.11(5) claims to have removed: "The nine now resolve to real levels, and the five kinds §0C.9 named become emittable." They do not. The build assertion at line 1471 cannot catch it: a constant `STEP_UP_VERIFIED` is ≥ every entry of `C9_FLOOR_BASELINE`, so the assertion passes vacuously while the floor is degenerate. This is round 7's defect class exactly — a declared type used as a different type, so a branch is silently dead — one function over from where round 7 fixed it.
structural.fix: Change the dispatcher at §0B.31 line 937 to `case 'C9': return c9Floor(ref);` and the build assertion at §0C.11(2) line 1471 to quantify over refs: `∀ key ∈ C9-CAP : c9Floor({ space: 'C9', key }) ≥ C9_FLOOR_BASELINE[key]`. Add the sibling assertion that actually bites — `|{ key ∈ C9-CAP : c9Floor({space:'C9',key}) === 'STEP_UP_VERIFIED' }| === 0` — so a future regression to the degenerate constant fails the build instead of passing it.

structural.clause: §0B.32, line 990: "**`WIDGET_CAPABILITY_POLICY` is keyed on `CapabilityRef`**, and is total over `C9_CAPABILITIES` (56 rows) only", with §0B.7, line 577: "every row key of `WIDGET_CAPABILITY_POLICY` ... are typed `CapabilityRef`, never `string`".
structural.conflictsWith: `CapabilityRef` is declared at §0B.7 lines 568–574 as a union of OBJECT types (`{ space: 'C9'; key: string } | { space: 'TOOL'; key: string } | { space: 'AE'; key: string } | { space: 'CONTROL'; key: ControlKey }`), and the table is bracket-indexed with an object at both live sites: §0C.10, line 1400: `const row = WIDGET_CAPABILITY_POLICY[ref];` and §0C.28-bis EC-11, line 2272: `→ WIDGET_CAPABILITY_POLICY[ref] must exist (else refuse), AND`. The contract states the governing rule itself, one erratum earlier — §0C.22-bis, line 1903: "// `InteractiveRef` is an object type and cannot key a Record, so the key form is declared" — and declares `refKey` for `InteractiveRef`, but declares no `capKey` for `CapabilityRef`. No errata row (§0.16, §0B.9, §0C.13) addresses the policy table's key type.
structural.consequence: A Record key must be `string | number | symbol`; `Readonly<Record<CapabilityRef, Row>>` is not constructible, and an object used as an index coerces to the single slot `"[object Object]"`. Every lookup therefore returns `undefined`. Two consequences, both in the newest text and both independent of structural violation #1: (a) in §0C.10's `c9Floor` the very next line is `if (row === undefined)  return 'STEP_UP_VERIFIED';      // FAIL CLOSED — unclassified (S0.15)`, so the replacement returns the unreachable constant for all 56 C9-CAP keys and EC-2's repair is undone a second time over; (b) EC-11's second Gate 6 C9 branch — the fence added specifically to cover the nine non-catalogue keys EC-2 made reachable — becomes an unconditional refusal of all nine, so §0C.32's claim that "what still fences these nine" includes "their `WIDGET_CAPABILITY_POLICY` row" names a lookup that can never succeed. Fail-closed in both cases, so no forbidden edge becomes constructible; but the two mechanisms EC-2 and EC-11 name do not do what their sentences say. The same defect also sits at §0B.31 line 944 (`WIDGET_CAPABILITY_POLICY[{ space: 'C9', key }]`, an object literal that would fail even against a Map, by reference identity) — that site is void under EC-2, which means EC-2 removed one instance of this defect and reintroduced it at line 1400.
structural.fix: Declare a total injective key function for capability refs exactly as §0C.22-bis declares `refKey` for `InteractiveRef` — `type CapabilityKey = \`${CapabilityRef['space']}:${string}\`; declare function capKey(ref: CapabilityRef): CapabilityKey;` with body `\`${ref.space}:${ref.key}\`` (total over the closed four-member union, injective because `space` is one of four fixed tokens and ':' is the only separator) — retype the table as `Readonly<Record<CapabilityKey, WidgetCapabilityPolicyRow>>`, amend §0B.32 and §0B.7 to say the table is keyed through `capKey`, and index through it at §0C.10 line 1400 and §0C.28-bis line 2272. Add the build assertion `keys(WIDGET_CAPABILITY_POLICY) === set(C9_CAPABILITIES.map(c => capKey({space:'C9', key: c.capabilityKey})))`, which makes §0B.32's totality-over-56 claim checkable instead of asserted.

structural.clause: §0C.17 `FLOOR_EXEMPT`, lines 1689–1692: `&& (i.effect !== 'HANDOFF' || (i.target?.class === 's' && !CONSENT(i.handoff_capability_ref) && !IDENTITY(i.handoff_capability_ref)));`, and the sentence it licenses at §0C.17-ter, lines 1721–1723: "`CONSENT` and `IDENTITY` (§0B.20, §0B.25) are now explicit exclusions from the predicate, so no consent or identity handoff is ever exempt, whatever its priority."
structural.conflictsWith: §0B.20, line 716, declares the predicate over a REGISTRY ROW, not over a ref: "Define, over `RegisteredActionCapabilityV1`: CONSENT(cap) := cap.targetKind ∈ {'client_consent', 'client_consent_security'} ∨ cap.actionClass ∈ {'record_client_consent', 'invalidate_client_consent_authority'}"; §0B.25 declares `IDENTITY(cap)` the same way; and §0B.16 exercises both with `cap` ranging over `new ActionCapabilityRegistry().list()`. But §0C.17's own `MintedIntent` declaration, line 1674, types the argument `handoff_capability_ref: CapabilityRef | null`, and §0B.7 line 577 confirms it.
structural.consequence: A `CapabilityRef` declares exactly two members, `space` and `key`; it has no `targetKind` and no `actionClass`, so `CONSENT(i.handoff_capability_ref)` and `IDENTITY(i.handoff_capability_ref)` evaluate `undefined ∈ {…}` and are FALSE for every possible input. Even under the charitable reading that the ref is looked up first, §0B.7 confines a HANDOFF's `handoff_capability_ref` to space `'C9'` while CONSENT/IDENTITY range over AE-CAP, and I re-verified in process that AE-CAP ∩ C9-CAP = 0 — so the lookup fails for every constructible input and the predicates are false either way. Both exclusions are therefore inert: they exclude nothing. Concretely, a composer that sets `priority: 0` on a class-`s` HANDOFF whose `handoff_capability_ref` names a consent or identity change owner gets `FLOOR_EXEMPT === true` and a floor of `ANONYMOUS`, waiving `KIND_FLOOR`, `targetFloor('s') = SESSION_VERIFIED` and the subject term together. That directly contradicts §0B.20's restated FR-6a, which permits the consent affordance only as "a `HANDOFF` of class `s` to `shell.privacy` with `verification_floor ≥ SESSION_VERIFIED`", and on `CONSENT_STATE` / `IDENTITY_BINDING` it collides with §0.27's mint fence ("every intent whose `role` is not `'escape'` has a derived `verification_floor ≥ SESSION_VERIFIED`"), making both kinds unmintable whenever their mandatory handoff carries priority 0. This is not a conferral — R3.5.3 and Gate 13 give a HANDOFF no capability-invoker edge, and §0.31's routes re-check the principal proof at `EP-FETCH` — so it is not a security-contract violation; it is a fence that is stated and not built. It is also the exact failure mode §0C.1 quotes as this round's lesson: "A fence that holds because no current clause exercises the hole is not a fence." Here it does not hold even that far.
structural.fix: Express the exclusion over the space the ref actually inhabits. Either (a) exclude on the widget layer's own classification — `!['personal_data','identity_binding'].includes(WIDGET_CAPABILITY_POLICY[capKey(i.handoff_capability_ref)]?.consent_class ?? 'personal_data')`, fail-closed on an absent row, which is total over C9-CAP and is the column §0.42 and §A1.6.2 already use for exactly this purpose; or (b) if the AE predicates are wanted, route through the pairing table — `const ae = AE_PROPOSE_PAIRING.find(r => r.propose equals i.handoff_capability_ref)?.ae; !ae || (!CONSENT(aeCapBy(ae)) && !IDENTITY(aeCapBy(ae)))` — and say so. Then restate §0C.17-ter to match what the chosen predicate delivers, and add the build veto `FLOOR_EXEMPT(i) ∧ i.effect === 'HANDOFF' ⟹ the handoff's consent_class ∉ {personal_data, identity_binding}` so the claim is checked rather than asserted.

structural.clause: §0C.28 (EC-10), lines 2224–2226: "> **PR2 (a′), normative.** The emission validator refuses any intent whose `subjectCapability(i)` satisfies `RUN_OPENING` on an envelope whose `origin` is `PROACTIVE`. *Evaluation point:* `EP-MINT`."
structural.conflictsWith: §0.3, line 106, declares the only trigger union in the contract: `trigger: 'user_turn' | 'proactive' | 'system_reply';   // E`, on the `Origin` object. `PROACTIVE` (uppercase) is a member of no union anywhere in the artefact — grep over all 6164 lines returns exactly one occurrence, this one — and `origin` is an `Origin` object, never a trigger value. Every other statement of the same predicate is correct: §3.2.5 line 4180 ("emission validator keyed on `origin.trigger === 'proactive'`"), §4.9.1 line 5807 ("`origin.trigger === 'proactive'` ⇒ …"), §0.17 item 15 line 497, and §0.3's own two `// non-null iff trigger === 'proactive'` comments.
structural.consequence: As written the antecedent compares an object against a string literal that no union declares, so it is never true and PR2 (a′) never refuses anything. EC-10 exists to replace PR2 mechanism (a), which it correctly voids because "the capability registry marks run-opening capabilities" would require a new `C9Capability` field and therefore change `C9_REGISTRY_HASH`. The replacement is well-founded — I confirmed in process that `mode` is a mandatory closed union and that `RUN_OPENING` selects exactly 15 of 56 (13 PROPOSE_ONLY + 2 OWNER_HANDOFF) — but it is delivered through a dead predicate, so after EC-10 the proactive envelope has no live run-opener fence at `EP-MINT`. PR1's effect ceiling (§4.9.1) and PR2 (b)'s standing CI leak query survive independently, so this weakens a fence rather than opening a forbidden edge; but §0C.32 lists EC-10 under "voids an unbuildable claim" while its own replacement is, as spelled, unbuildable in the same way. This is the spelling defect class round 7 filed and repaired — it survived at this one site, in Section 0-C, the newest text.
structural.fix: Rewrite the antecedent as `origin.trigger === 'proactive'`, matching §3.2.5, §4.9.1 and §0.3. Add the documentation-link/spelling test §0.1 already commissions in the same form: a build assertion that every value literal quoted in a normative predicate is a declared member of the union it is compared against — which would have caught this and would catch the next one.

unproven.clause: §0C.28-ter (EC-11), lines 2292–2302, the declaration of `IntentRecord.c9_domain`: "Mint class D, AUDIT_RETAINED. Non-null IFF `capability.space === 'C9'`. **Derived at EP-MINT from the emitting run's registered agent domain; on the capability-read path, where `run_ref` is null, from the resolved principal's domain.** NEVER from the subject capability's own `domains` — that would compare a value with itself and make the test vacuous." §0C.28-ter's own justification for adding the field is that "A gate cannot pass an argument the record does not carry", and it is the argument EC-11's second Gate 6 branch feeds to `c9Capability(record.capability.key, record.c9_domain, C9_REGISTRY_HASH)`.
unproven.whyUnproven: The second half of the derivation names a member that no principal shape declares, in the contract or in the repository. §1.7 K3 enumerates the principal exactly — `c9PrincipalHash(principal)` is "a digest over `kind`, `tenantId`, `userId`, `membershipId`, `clientId`, `channelLinkId`, `branchRefs`, `staffRef` and `proofHash`" — nine members, no domain. I loaded the repository types in process: `C9Principal` (`src/orchestration/c9.contract.ts:197–207`) declares exactly those nine and no domain; `AiToolPrincipal` (`src/ai-tools/ai-tool.types.ts`) declares `tenantId`, `userId`, `role`, `surface` and no domain; `C9Authority.current` (`src/orchestration/c9.authority.ts:20–50`) constructs both branches without one. In the repository a `C9Domain` attaches to an objective (`C9_ROUTES`, `c9.contract.ts:25`), to an agent (`c9.agents.ts:60–67`) and to a capability (`def.domains`) — never to a principal. §0C.28-ter's own survey concedes the point one sentence earlier: "A full read of the contract finds **exactly one** domain-valued member anywhere — `Correlation.agent_id` (§1.1.4), which is envelope-level, nullable, and named by no gate. `IntentRecord` declares none." It then names a second source that does not exist, while expressly forbidding the one value that could be computed from what the record does carry. The `NORMATIVE-PENDING` marking on EC-11 (P-01, P-26) and the addition of the field to P-30's component list do not cover this: those prerequisites are the gateway, its Gate 6 dispatch and the gateway's record fields, and building any of them cannot create a `domain` member on a principal type this contract does not own and does not propose to change (FR-16, §0.3). This is the same defect class EC-6 was written to close — a mechanism whose CI check names `intent.utterance`, a member `WidgetIntent` does not declare — reproduced inside EC-11's own repair.
unproven.fix: Derive `c9_domain` from a member the contract actually declares. The cleanest route is already ruled on: §0.16 E-29 reclassifies `Correlation.agent_id` as class **D**, "derived by the minter from the run's registered agent", and its union is the same four `C9Domain` tokens — so make `correlation.agent_id` non-null whenever an intent of `capability.space === 'C9'` is minted, and set `c9_domain = correlation.agent_id`, with the `EP-MINT` refusal keyed on that. If the capability-read path genuinely has no agent, register a widget-layer `PRINCIPAL_DOMAIN_RESOLVER` (or a fixed read-path domain) as a new prerequisite row with its own `MG-` gap key under §0C.20's ledger, and bind this clause to it — so that until it ships the read path refuses rather than silently having no derivable value.
